page.layout: One text block of two paragraphs, below two coin engravings at the top. No marginal notes. Running head at the top with the page number to its left.

main_text.l: NICEPHORVS Patricius, relegata Irene, Constantino-
politanum imperiũ invadit anno mundi 4764. à Christo nato
802. Hic fœdus cum Carolo magno icit. Nemo maiore opinio-
ne hominum ad imperium venit, dum singulos aut muliebris
impotentiæ, aut flagitiosi principis tædet: nemo tamen avarius
aut crudelius administravit: quorũ scelerum mox pœnas meri-
tas luit. A Bulgaris enim paulò ante à se victis, improviso noctis
assultu oppressus, ipse cum toto exercitu ad internecionem cæ-
ditur. Stauracius filius faucius evadit, qui cum patre impera-
rat, & post patrem Imperator ab amicis salutatus, non multò
post à Michaële Curoplate, qui sororem eius in vxorem duxe-
rat, imperio deturbatur, & monasterio includitur. Vide Blon.
lib.2. Egn. lib. 2. Stauracius in hac Imperatorum serie minimè
à nobis inseritur, quòd paucis diebus post Nicephorum pa-
trem imperitarit.
MICHAEL Curoplates, Rangabe cognomento, imper-
arat, qua dixi via, Constantinopoli anno mundi 4773. à Chri-
sto nato 811. hic melior pacis artibus & pietate, quàm bellicis
rebus administrandis, ad unam adversam cum Bulgaris pu-
gnam, ita deiecit animũ, ut accepto nuntio de Leonis imperio,
qui post eum Constantinopoli imperat, monasterio sese abdi-
derit: habenas imperij facilè relinquens post annum alterum
imperij. Hic quemadmodum Nicephorus, legaris ad Carolum
magnum missis pacem fecit, hac conditione ut Veneti suis le-
gibus ac iure viverent: immunitate his servata, quam ad eam
diem retinuerant. Egn.lib.2.

page.notes: Two engravings of coins at the top of the page, not text. Left: a double portrait with the legend "D N NICEFORVS IMP" and "TAVRI TIVS AVG" (the second legend reads in reverse at the bottom), the obverse of Nicephorus and Stauracius. Right: a portrait with the legend "D N MICHAEL AVG", with a small ornament below the bust. Printed text is not reproduced in the engraving legends above; they are part of the image. Doubtful: the regnal year figure at the end of the Michael paragraph is printed as "4773" with a worn final digit, read as 3. No other doubtful readings.
